Regular morning mist-netting used 70–150 m in low cover southwest and sparse scrub south of the lodge; nets were erected before dawn and dismantled after operations because of large game.
Night nets were added below the floodlights; the decoded site field contains an unresolved 1974 discrepancy.

The number and wattage of north-facing lights were often reduced to save electricity and because of breakdowns; this was reported to reduce attraction. Dates identify the covered 1982 session, not individual affected nights.
Night netting was possible on only seven nights during the reported session; suitable conditions rather than a fixed nightly schedule determined operation.
Fewer birds were reported attracted after replacement of the main lamps.
Twenty-five nights were spent at the lodge and suitable weather allowed catching attempts on 18; this is coverage evidence rather than a daily operation record.
Broad configuration period; nightly availability is unknown.
Ringers spent 19 nights at Ngulia and catching was possible on all but four; dates represent the reported coverage interval rather than consecutive nightly deployment.
The team erected its own 1 kW light north of the lodge during the early-December period to compensate for reduced or failed lodge lights; exact installation and removal dates are not reported.
Twenty-seven nights in two periods were spent at Ngulia and birds were caught and ringed on 23 dates; this is not a complete daily effort calendar.

Torrential rain on the night of 6/7 December and throughout 7 December severely curtailed netting; retain the two-date interval because the source reports an overnight event. The combined overnight/day event is assigned once to ringing date 7 December for daily use.
Visits covered 23 days and most nights did not develop mist at lodge level; the low catch should not be interpreted as a fixed reduction in effort.
The report specifies 27 m of night net erected after mist descended at 01:30; it is an event-specific configuration observation.
November small-moon visits had clear nights and no netting; exact November dates are not given and this row must not be joined as daily data.
Broad configuration period; nightly availability is unknown.

The two small-moon coverage periods were 14–28 November and 11–23 December; 25 participants allowed three 18 m mist-nets almost every night. The enclosing interval is contextual and not a continuous deployment record.
The season comprised two sessions (5–16 November and 30 November–17 December) and 30 days of coverage; intermediate dates must not be assumed to have been manned.

The synthesis describes a 1994 move to northern/front bush, routine in 1995; its map labels the old southern area 1972–1994. DJP B refers to back bush, not the later northern back line. Retain transition uncertainty; daily F records identify actual northern use.

The third northern net line was extended by five nets, bringing the ENTIRE northern arrangement to 270 m (not the back line alone). It could be omitted when staffing or catch volume constrained operations. This is not the DJP B/back-bush site code.
Reference configuration only; individual nightly availability is unknown.
Two project 1 kW lights were used each night while lodge lights suffered frequent breakdowns.
Three night nets operated from 00:20 to 05:20; the L and mid-line dawn nets opened at 05:50 and 06:15 and were closed by rain at 09:00.
Temporary lodge lights were substituted; exact affected dates are not reported.
Report-based habitat condition rather than a measured cover estimate.
The report explicitly links elephant thinning to reduced dawn-catching potential.
The report dates the all-floodlight electrical failure to the night of 16 December.
Report estimate; not mapped vegetation cover.
On the first night of the reported session only one working floodlight had been set up. Source night begins on arrival 25 November; applies to ringing morning 26 November.
The next day three floodlights were assembled using new cables: 1.5 kW, 1 kW and 1 kW. This is a setup event, not proof of uninterrupted availability thereafter.
One main lodge circuit failed and cable connections were rearranged; exact dates need extraction before daily use.
Three floodlights assembled using new cables; two new lamps were 1.5 and 1 kW.
Three working lamps were documented as 2 x 1 kW and 1 x 1.5 kW.
The project depended mainly on three halogen lamps providing 3.5 kW in total.
Report directly links vegetation loss and sparse cover to lower daytime catch potential.
Availability and planning delays restricted the project to one December session; the lodge was manned 6–20 December and daily team size is not recorded.
Textual evidence includes night and hirundine lures; dates species and timing require event-level extraction.
Textual evidence includes taped Sprosser and Marsh Warbler songs; exact dates can be extracted in a later event-level pass.
The diary records Marsh and Sprosser tapes on from 02:00; use is explicit but the preceding-night date convention should be retained in any daily join.
Mist lowered at 01:30; the second night net was erected at 02:00 and both night nets closed at 04:15.
Night nets were closed at 23:45 and 01:00 because of heavy rain and reopened at 00:15 and 01:20 before final closure at 03:20.
The L and Niko nets closed at 09:00 because of team size and the number of birds; six to eight nets reopened from 11:00.
Two night nets were furled at 02:30 because of small team size and catch volume; dawn L and Niko nets closed at 07:30.
A strong westerly wind and persistent rain followed a brief net reopening; night nets were not reopened again and were taken down before dawn.
Heavy rain closed night nets at 00:30 before reopening at 01:00; heavy rain also curtailed swallow-net ringing at 10:20.
Heavy rain closed night nets at 00:30; they reopened at 01:00 and closed at 03:00 after catching slowed.
Day nets were taken down after the morning operation; the remaining party used one night net on 7 December.
No further elephant damage and slow regrowth were reported.
Floodlights were prepared for the session with new bulbs fitted; fixture model spectrum output and nightly availability remain unreported.
The northern netting bush was reported to have regenerated well.
Rains supported grass and herb cover plus regeneration of smaller bushes.
The report describes opening of formerly thick bush and flattening of tall trees by elephants.
Financial restrictions associated with COVID limited the operation to a ten-day visit, reported as the shortest session since 1969.
Electricity was restored after midnight before night nets opened.
Night nets opened at 00:45 because of generator problems.
Night nets opened at 02:00 because of the continuing generator problem; rain later curtailed dawn activity.
Report describes improved ability of habitat to hold migrants.
Hotel guests prevented night nets opening until after midnight; only half the bush nets were initially available and rain closed the remaining nets from 09:00.
Night netting was curtailed at 02:25 partly because of a leopard near the nets and dawn bush-net opening was delayed by 30 minutes.
Abundant Red-billed Queleas forced early closure of the nets at 10:30.
Night nets did not open until 03:00; rain forced closure after one hour and only another 45 minutes of netting was possible before dawn.
Overnight rain never became light enough for night nets to open; the sole night capture was by hand.
Policy statement for nocturnal migrants; targeted diurnal lures remain a distinct exposure.

The night after lamps were assembled on 26 November produced about 40 birds despite taped sound; about 140 at dawn identifies ringing date 27 November (workbook total 184). This overrides workbook blank-to-absence, without inferring speaker location.
Report explicitly describes attempts to attract daytime swallows with tapes after the 27/28 November night.
Report dates circuit rearrangement to 29 November and states that two lamps were on during night netting; no assumption about duration of the outage.
138 Barn Swallows caught after attraction to taped sound. Confirms diurnal playback and swallow nets; do not infer nocturnal playback.
Four hours of night catching with all three lamps up and running; this is direct nightly evidence, unlike the earlier assembly event.
Swallows attracted again and over 300 ringed during the morning.
Final night session thwarted by clear sky; bush nets had been dismantled the previous morning. Confirms workbook non-operation and its recorded zero.
